unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: We are interested in the asymptotic behavior of estimators when $n\to\infty$, $T\to\infty$, and $\rho\to0$. It is perhaps the easiest to relate $L$ and $\rho$ to $n$ by considering sequences $(T_n,\rho_n)_{n=1}^\infty$, which makes it more natural to write the corresponding mixture model sequence $P_{1,n}=P_1(n,T_n,\rho_n)$, and $P_{0,n}=P_0(n,T_n,\rho_n)$ as in Definition 1.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Source sequence convention, retaining the stray L in the prose. Assumption1 is explicitly invoked by Conjecture3.2 and Theorems3.3/4.2; Theorems3.1/4.1 state their own sufficient threshold conditions without that numbered reference.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Lemma 2.1 (Detection implies recovery). Under the MLSBM specified in Definition 1, if $P_{1,n}$ is asymptotically recoverable for a sequence $(T_n,\rho_n)$, then it is distinguishable for $(T_n+2,\rho_n)$ with polynomial additional computing time.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: The caption reverses the implication actually stated: recovery implies detection, with two additional layers. The main-text discussion says this change does not affect the considered asymptotic thresholds. Preserve the direction and layer change; do not add a sixth Theorem or an implication-only definition edge.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: As detailed in the proof, the exponent of $-1.4$ can be improved to $-1.01$ if $T_n\gg\log^{2.02}n$. Here the notion of “polynomial-time” means polynomial in $n$, because when $\rho_n$ satisfies Assumption 1, the condition $nT_n^{1/2}\rho_n\le(1/2)(\log n)^{1.4}$ implies $T_n=O(n^2)$ and hence the total size of $A$ is polynomial in $n$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Prose following Theorem3.3, not part of its italic theorem statement. It prints a positive log exponent in the input-size explanation, unlike the theorem’s negative exponent; preserve and flag that discrepancy. The improved threshold requires an extra layer-growth condition and is not inserted into the theorem.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: The original version of the conjecture in [20] is more general and requires various forms of regularity conditions. These conditions can be directly verified for our MLSBM sequence $(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})_{n\ge1}$ specified in Definition 1 with $(T_n,\rho_n)$ satisfying Assumption 1.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Remark1 asserts applicability of the externally cited conjecture’s regularity conditions. The main text does not enumerate those conditions; the current census preserves the specialized Conjecture3.2 and does not certify the external assertion.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Recall that for two sequences of probability distributions, $(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})_{n\in\mathbb N}$, over a common sequence of measurable spaces, we say $P_{1,n}$ is contiguous to $P_{0,n}$, if for any sequence of events $(E_n:n\ge1)$, $P_{0,n}(E_n)\to0$ implies $P_{1,n}(E_n)\to0$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Contiguity is explanatory context in Remark2, not a premise of Theorems2.2 or3.3 and not the same as vanishing chi-square divergence. Do not add it as a dependency simply because it motivates low-degree hardness.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: the computation thresholds for detection and recovery in the multi-layer stochastic block model. The computational upper bound for recovery (and hence detection) has been studied in [28, 29], in which a variant of spectral clustering was proved to consistently recover the membership when $nT_n^{1/2}\rho_n\gtrsim O(\sqrt{\log(n)})$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: External algorithmic provenance for Theorem3.1; the main text does not give the algorithm’s complete construction. Preserve the theorem’s existence statement and exact threshold without inventing a local spectral-estimator definition.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: These two priors can be changed to the corresponding Bernoulli models (i.e., $\sigma(i)\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)$) with additional bookkeeping.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Discussed alternative priors, not the exact balanced priors in Definition1. No new theorem or mathematically equivalent prior variant is inferred.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Unlike the MLE considered in Section 4.2, the bias-adjusted spectral method works for a more general class of MLSBMs, allowing $B_t$ to vary arbitrarily as long as $T_n^{-1}\rho_n^{-2}\sum_tB_t^2\succeq cI$ for some positive constant $c$. It would be interesting to develop a corresponding method for the information-theoretic upper bound that works for such more general MLSBMs.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Discussion of broader models and future work. The theorems here are for the special balanced mixture; do not transfer their information-theoretic conclusions to arbitrary layer matrices.

source_issues.note: P1,n is explicitly called the joint law of (A,sigma,tau), and P1,tau,n the conditional joint law of (A,sigma). Testing and chi-square formulas instead use their A marginals, as the explicit sum over A demonstrates. The null law is on A only. Preserve the original notation while keeping the sample spaces separate.

Uniform priors are on exactly balanced node and layer assignments, not iid Bernoulli labels. The generative list gives separate prior draws without explicitly writing their independence; the natural product-prior interpretation is recorded as such. Edge independence holds conditional on latent assignments, not under their marginal mixture.

The general model uses labels in [K], then the K=2 specialization uses {0,1}. Edges are observed only for i<j, with symmetric matrices and no modeled self-loops. The MLE parity sum inherits those index ranges. Recovery is invariant to the global node-label complement.

Both n and T must be even, while Theorem2.2 writes T_n=n^a for arbitrary a>0. Appropriate subsequences or rounding are implicit. Its inequalities are strict and make no claim on 1+a−b=0 or1+a/2−b=0. Assumption1 is stronger than just rho_n→0, and threshold limits nT rho and n sqrt(T) rho must remain distinct.

The computational impossibility statements depend on the specialized low-degree polynomial conjecture. The conjecture tests uniform boundedness over all centered null-L2-normalized polynomials of degree at most log^1.01(n); boundedness for a single polynomial is insufficient. It is not a proved impossibility theorem or P-versus-NP result.

Recoverability means vanishing normalized Hamming fraction in probability under the mixture prior, not exact recovery or a uniform fixed-label minimax guarantee. Distinguishability means vanishing total testing error. Failure of that property alone does not imply failure of every weak test; Theorem4.1 separately establishes the stronger vanishing chi-square result.

Lemma2.1 is captioned Detection implies recovery, but its actual statement is recovery implies detection with T_n+2 layers and polynomial extra work. The source says the two-layer change is negligible for its threshold regimes. No reversed reduction or same-finite-T identity is inserted.

The prose assigns q,p to P,Q respectively, while the displayed d_chi2(Q,P)=E_P[(q/p−1)^2] requires q for Q and p for P. Preserve the printed mismatch and use the theorem’s explicit null-denominator formula to identify the intended direction. P0 has positive mass on every observed tensor when0<rho<2/3.

Theorem4.1 quantifies over every balanced tau in S_Tn while summing the A-marginal likelihood ratio. It keeps sigma unobserved even when tau is known. Balanced layer permutations make these cases symmetric; do not reinterpret the claim as observing both sigma and tau.

Theorem3.3 has threshold (1/2)(log n)^−1.4, but the following runtime explanation prints exponent+1.4. Its claimed T_n=O(n²) does not follow from that weaker positive-exponent condition alone; the actual negative-exponent theorem condition does support polynomial input size. Preserve both passages and the distinct optional −1.01 improvement. The n-based runtime convention is stated in the lower-bound discussion; its relation to input-size complexity for unrestricted layer growth in the upper-bound result is not fully specified locally.

Equation(4) jointly optimizes balanced sigma and tau by counting edges on even-parity triples. A choice among ties is not specified. Theorem4.2 asserts approximate consistency for sigma only; it supplies neither a polynomial-time implementation nor a claim of consistent tau recovery.

Theorem3.1 credits[28] and refers to an externally developed spectral method without defining it completely. Remark1 claims external conjecture regularity can be verified but does not list it. Retain these source limitations; neither missing implementation details nor a conjecture becomes an invented locally verified API.

T2.2.parameters: T_n=n^a, rho_n=n^−b, a>0,0<b<2; positive even dimensions implicit.

branches.information_theoretic: No computational constraint; strict sign of1+a−b. No conjecture premise.
branches.computational: Conjecture3.2 is assumed in the second bullet; strict sign of1+a/2−b. The credited computational upper result3.1 is itself unconditional.

T3.1.parameters: n*sqrt(T_n)*rho_n≥C*sqrt(log n), some absolute C>0; Definition1 model and source sequence context.
T3.1.conclusion: Existence of a polynomial-time recovery algorithm; its full construction is external, not reconstructed from a name.

T3.3.parameters: Definition1 model; Assumption1 and Conjecture3.2; negative-log threshold eventually.
T3.3.conclusion: Conditional impossibility of strong polynomial-time detection. Main-text optional exponent improvement is not part of the original theorem statement.

T4.1.parameters: Definition1 observation experiment; n*T_n*rho_n→0; every balanced tau.
T4.1.conclusion: Known-tau alternative A-marginal chi-square tends to zero; then mixed alternative chi-square tends to zero and strong detection fails. No hardness conjecture.

T4.2.conclusion: Joint-MLE sigma component has vanishing normalized Hamming fraction for every epsilon>0, hence asymptotic recovery and detection. No polynomial runtime assertion or tau-consistency conclusion.
